summary: Active in Tibetology and other fields, Aung San Suu Kyi studied at the University of Delhi, Lady Shri Ram College, St Hugh's College, and SOAS University of London. She held a post at the United Nations from around 1969 to 1971.

A scholar of Japanology, Axel Klein studied at the University of Bonn (1987–1994). He served as a wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at Bonn (1998–2007) and the German Institute for Japanese Studies (2007–2011), and became a professor at the University of Duisburg-Essen in 2012.

Axel Michaels works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg and Kiel University under Laxmi Nath Shrestha. He directed the Nepal Research Centre, held a professorship at the University of Bern, and became professor at Heidelberg University in 1996.

Ayu Khandro was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Drodul Pawo Dorje, Nyala Pema Dündul, and Chokgyur Lingpa, and later taught A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé and Namkhai Norbu.

Ayya Khema worked in Buddhist and religious studies, training under Laurence Khantipalo Mills, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, and Matara Sri Ñāṇarāma. She founded Wat Buddha Dhamma in 1978 and Sakyadhita in 1987, and taught at Buddha-Haus from 1989.

B. Alan Wallace works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Amherst College and Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and traditional Tibetan masters, he taught at Rabten Choeling and UC Santa Barbara, and founded the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies.

B. N. K. Sharma was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his degrees at the University of Madras while studying under Satyadhyana Tirtha. He served as principal of Rajah's College and Poornaprajna Sanskrit College, and retired as Professor of Samskrit from Ramnarain Ruia College.

B. R. Ambedkar worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Columbia University, the London School of Economics, and Gray's Inn under scholars including John Dewey. He served as professor at Sydenham College and principal of Government Law College, Mumbai.

Baatr Kitinov is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. in World History from Moscow State University and serves as an Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra was an Indologist and archaeologist. Educated at Panjab University and Leiden University, he served as Government Epigraphist for India, Assistant and Joint Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India, and later as Professor at Panjab University.

Baiei Henmi was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University from around 1914 to 1918, held a post at Tama Art University, and taught Osamu Takata.

Baihui Wu was an Indologist and philosopher. He worked at Visva-Bharati University (ca. 1945–1951), served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University (ca. 1952–1956), and held research posts at the Institute of Philosophy and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Baij Nath Puri was an Indian historian and Indologist. He earned his M.Litt. and D.Phil. at the University of Oxford and served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow from around 1971 to 1976.

Bal Gangadhar Tilak worked in Indology and history. He studied at Deccan College and Government Law College, Mumbai. He co-founded the New English School, where he taught, as well as Fergusson College, where he served as a mathematics teacher from around 1885 to 1890.

Bal Krishen Thapar was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Panjab University, under Mortimer Wheeler at Taxila, and at Heidelberg. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981) and later chaired the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training.
Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist who worked at Panjab University, where he is attested as an Assistant in 1932 and as in-charge of the Sanskrit Section in 1941.

Bangwei Wang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Peking University between 1983 and 1987 and served there as a professor, including as Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies, around 1992.

Banikanta Kakati was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Educated at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, he served as a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and later as Dean of Arts and Head of Assamese at Gauhati University.

Bapudeva Sastri was an Indologist who studied at Sehore High School under Lancelot Wilkinson, as well as under Dhundiraja Misra and Sevarama. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

Barbara E. Ward worked in Sinology and related fields. Educated at Newnham College, London, and the LSE, she taught history at the University of London, lectured at Cambridge, was a fellow at Clare Hall and Newnham, and held visiting professorships at Cornell and CUHK.
